items.name: directed preorder
items.statement_summary: A preorder P is directed when any two elements p,q have a common upper bound r (p<=r and q<=r), r not required unique; equivalently every finite subset (including the empty one, so P is nonempty) has an upper bound. Also called a directed set.

items.name: filtered category
items.statement_summary: A category J is filtered when J is nonempty and: (a) for any two objects j,j' there is an object k with arrows j->k and j'->k; (b) for any two parallel arrows u,v: i->j there is an arrow w: j->k with wu=wv. Generalizes 'directed preorder' from posets to categories.

items.name: finite diagrams have cocones in a filtered category
items.statement_summary: Consequence of the filtered axioms: condition (a) makes a two-object discrete diagram the base of a cocone and (b) makes a parallel pair the base of a cocone, so every finite diagram in a filtered category J is the base of at least one cocone with some vertex k in J.

items.name: filtered colimit
items.statement_summary: A filtered colimit is, by definition, a colimit of a functor F: J->C whose domain category J is filtered (generalizing colimits over directed preorders).

items.name: coproducts from finite coproducts and directed colimits
items.statement_summary: A category C that has finite coproducts and colimits over all small directed preorders has all small coproducts. (Proof: index the poset J+ of finite subsets of the index set J, take a finite coproduct over each subset, and realize the desired coproduct as the directed colimit of these over J+.)

items.name: forgetful Grp->Set creates filtered colimits
items.statement_summary: The forgetful functor Grp->Set creates filtered colimits: for a filtered diagram of groups, the colimit of the underlying sets carries a unique group structure making the injections group homomorphisms, and this group is the colimit in Grp. The argument uses only that J is filtered.

items.name: creation of filtered colimits generalizes to algebras of a type
items.statement_summary: The proof of Proposition 2 (and Corollary 3) is not restricted to Grp: it applies to Alg_tau, the category of algebras of any fixed operator-and-identity type tau (as in V.6). Thus the forgetful functor Alg_tau->Set creates filtered colimits, and Alg_tau has all small colimits.

items.name: Grp is cocomplete
items.statement_summary: Grp has all small colimits. (The one-element group is initial; two groups have a coproduct, the free product G*H, verified via the solution-set/adjoint-functor route with G->G*H monic; coequalizers exist as quotient groups H->H/N; Proposition 2 gives filtered colimits; Theorem 1 then yields all small coproducts, hence all small colimits.)

items.name: adjoint-functor-theorem proof that Grp is cocomplete
items.statement_summary: Exercise: use the adjoint functor theorem to prove in one step that Grp has all small colimits.

items.name: Alg_tau is cocomplete
items.statement_summary: Exercise: prove that Alg_tau, as described in V.6, has all small colimits; in particular describe its initial object and determine when it is empty.

items.name: iterated colimits commute (and dually iterated limits)
items.statement_summary: For a bifunctor F: P x J -> X with X cocomplete, forming Colim_j F(p,j) is functorial in p (colimiting cones natural in p, by Thm V.3.1) and iterated colimits interchange via a canonical iso: Colim_p Colim_j F(p,j) ~= Colim_j Colim_p F(p,j) (proved in section 8). Dually, iterated limits commute. Limits need NOT commute with colimits.

items.name: canonical map colim-lim -> lim-colim
items.statement_summary: For F: P x J -> X, whenever all four iterated (co)limits exist there is a canonical arrow kappa: Colim_j Lim_p F(p,j) -> Lim_p Colim_j F(p,j), built from the limiting cones v and colimiting cones mu by their universal properties (diagram 4). It need not be an isomorphism (counterexample: P,J both the discrete 2-object category in Set, where the domain is a 2-fold and codomain a 4-fold disjoint union; it IS iso in Ab).

items.name: finite limits commute with filtered colimits in Set
items.statement_summary: If P is finite and J is small and filtered, then for every bifunctor F: P x J -> Set the canonical arrow kappa: Colim_j Lim_p F(p,j) -> Lim_p Colim_j F(p,j) is an isomorphism; i.e. finite limits commute with filtered colimits in Set. (Proof constructs a two-sided inverse using the finite-diagram-has-a-cocone property of filtered J.)
flags: text says 'as in (iv)', apparently a typo for diagram (4)/(3)

items.name: naturality of the canonical map kappa
items.statement_summary: Exercise: show that the canonical map kappa of (3) is natural for arrows sigma: F => F' in the functor category X^{P x J}.

items.name: pseudo-filtered categories (Verdier)
items.statement_summary: Exercise (Verdier), which also DEFINES 'pseudo-filtered': J is pseudo-filtered if it satisfies condition (b) for filtered categories plus (a'): any two arrows i->j, i->j' with common domain embed in a commutative diamond. Prove J is filtered iff it is connected and pseudo-filtered, and that J is pseudo-filtered iff each of its connected components is filtered.
flags: defines pseudo-filtered category inside the exercise

items.name: coproducts commute with pullback in Set
items.statement_summary: Exercise: in Set, show that coproducts commute with pullback.

items.name: pseudo-filtered colimits commute with pullbacks in Set
items.statement_summary: Exercise: using Exercises 2 and 3, show that pseudo-filtered colimits commute with pullbacks in Set.

items.name: final functor
items.statement_summary: A functor L: J' -> J is final if for every object k in J the comma category (k \downarrow L) is nonempty and connected: there exist j' in J' and an arrow k -> Lj', and any two such arrows are joined by a finite zig-zag of commuting triangles under k. (Classical term: cofinal.)

items.name: final subcategory
items.statement_summary: A subcategory is final when its inclusion functor is final; e.g. for J a linear order, J' subset of J is final iff every k in J has some j' in J' with k <= j'.

items.name: canonical comparison colim FL -> colim F
items.statement_summary: For L: J' -> J and F: J -> X there is a canonical map h: Colim FL -> Colim F, defined when both colimits exist as the unique arrow with h . mu'_{j'} = mu_{Lj'} for all j' in J', where mu, mu' are the colimiting cones.

items.name: final functors preserve and detect colimits
items.statement_summary: If L: J' -> J is final and F: J -> X is a functor such that x = Colim FL exists, then Colim F also exists and the canonical map h: Colim FL -> Colim F is an isomorphism. Thus colimits may be computed over final subcategories. (Finality is necessary, cf. Exercise 5.)

items.name: dual notion: initial functors and limits
items.statement_summary: The dual of a final functor is an 'initial' functor; the dual of Theorem 1 states that limits may be computed over initial subcategories (limits are unchanged along initial functors). The finality/initiality hypothesis is necessary.

items.name: one-object inclusion is final iff terminal
items.statement_summary: Exercise: for j in J, the inclusion of the one-object discrete subcategory {j} -> J is final iff j is a terminal object of J; interpret the consequence for colimits and terminal objects.

items.name: composite of final functors is final
items.statement_summary: Exercise: prove that a composite of final functors is final.

items.name: full functor into a filtered category with nonempty commas is final
items.statement_summary: Exercise: if J is filtered, L: J' -> J is full, and each comma category (k \downarrow L) is nonempty (for k in J), prove that L is final.

items.name: colimit of a covariant hom-functor is a point
items.statement_summary: Exercise: for the covariant hom-functor J(k,-): J -> Set, use the Yoneda Lemma to show that Colim J(k,-) is the one-point set.

items.name: converse: comparison-iso for all X implies final
items.statement_summary: Exercise (converse of Theorem 1): let L: J' -> J with J', J having small colimits, such that for every cocomplete X and every F the canonical map Colim FL -> Colim F is an isomorphism; prove L must be final (hint: take F = J(k,-), X = Set, and Exercise 4).

items.name: dinatural transformation
items.statement_summary: For functors S,T: C^op x C -> B, a dinatural transformation alpha: S => T assigns to each object c an arrow alpha_c: S(c,c) -> T(c,c) such that for every f: c -> c' the hexagon commutes: T(1,f) . alpha_c . S(f,1) = T(f,1) . alpha_{c'} . S(1,f) as arrows S(c',c) -> T(c,c'). Every ordinary natural transformation restricts to a dinatural one on the diagonal (alpha_c = tau_{c,c}). A dummy special case (S dummy in 2nd, T dummy in 1st variable) yields a 'natural transformation of a contravariant functor to a covariant functor' (square 2).

items.name: dummy (constant-in-a-variable) functor
items.statement_summary: A functor T: C^op x C -> B is dummy in a variable if it factors through the projection deleting that variable (so it is essentially a one-variable functor); dummy in both variables means constant at an object b in B (T(c,c') = b and T(f,f') = 1_b for all arrows).

items.name: wedge / extranatural transformation
items.statement_summary: When T = b is constant, a dinatural transformation alpha: S => b (components alpha_c: S(c,c) -> b with alpha_c . S(f,1) = alpha_{c'} . S(1,f) for f: c -> c', square 3) is called an extranatural / supernatural transformation, or a wedge, from S to b. Dually a wedge beta: b => T has components beta_c: b -> T(c,c) satisfying T(1,f) . beta_c = T(f,1) . beta_{c'} (square 4).

items.name: Euclid: natural self-duality as a dinatural transformation
items.statement_summary: Illustrative example (type-2 dinatural): the category Euclid of Euclidean spaces (real vector spaces with a bilinear symmetric positive-definite inner product) and inner-product-preserving linear maps, with forgetful U: Euclid -> Vct_R and dual *: Euclid^op -> Vct_R; the canonical maps kappa_E: E -> E* are the components of a dinatural transformation kappa: U => * expressing that each Euclidean space is naturally isomorphic to its dual.

items.name: evaluation is an extranatural transformation
items.statement_summary: For a fixed set A, evaluation V_X: hom(X,A) x X -> A, <h,x> |-> h x, gives the components of an extranatural transformation (wedge) V: hom(-,A) x (-) => A from the bifunctor hom(-,A) x (-): Set^op x Set -> Set to A; it is also natural in the parameter A.

items.name: counit of a parametrized adjunction is extranatural in the parameter
items.statement_summary: For an adjunction with parameter (natural bijection A(F(x,p),a) ~= X(x,G(p,a)) natural in x,p,a; F: X x P -> A, G: P^op x A -> X; Thm IV.7.3), setting x = G(p,a) yields the counit components eps_{<p,a>}: F(G(p,a),p) -> a, which are natural in a and dinatural (extranatural) in the parameter p. Evaluation is the special case.

items.name: identity arrows form a dinatural transformation
items.statement_summary: In any category C the identities 1_c in hom(c,c), regarded as arrows 1_c: * -> hom(c,c) from the one-point set, are the components of a dinatural (extranatural, dual type) transformation 1: * => hom(-,-) from the constant functor * to the hom-bifunctor hom(-,-): C^op x C -> Set; the wedge condition is exactly f . 1_c = 1_{c'} . f.

items.name: combined multi-variable (di)natural transformation
items.statement_summary: Unifying natural and dinatural transformations: for S: C^op x C x A -> B and T: A x D^op x D -> B, a natural transformation gamma: S => T assigns to each triple (c,a,d) an arrow gamma(c,a,d): S(c,c,a) -> T(a,d,d) that is (i) natural in a (fixed c,d), (ii) dinatural in c (fixed a,d), (iii) dinatural in d (fixed c,a). Naturality in a product argument may be replaced by separate naturality in each factor. All three types are jointly called 'natural transformations'.

items.name: dinatural transformations compose with genuinely natural ones
items.statement_summary: The composite of two dinatural transformations need not be dinatural, but any dinatural alpha: S => T may be composed on either side with transformations sigma: S' => S and tau: T => T' that are natural in both arguments, and the componentwise composite tau_c . alpha_c . sigma_c: S'(c,c) -> T'(c,c) is again dinatural, S' => T'.

items.name: diagonal composite of natural/dinatural families is natural
items.statement_summary: Given functors R: C -> B, S: C x C^op x C -> B, T: C -> B and families of arrows rho(c,d): R(c) -> S(c,d,d) and sigma(d,c): S(d,d,c) -> T(c), each natural in c and dinatural in d, the assignment c |-> [ R(c) --rho(c,c)--> S(c,c,c) --sigma(c,c)--> T(c) ] (the diagonal composite) is a natural transformation R => T.

items.name: unit of a parametrized adjunction is dinatural
items.statement_summary: Show the unit eta_x : x -> G(p, F(x,p)) of an adjunction with a parameter p is dinatural in p, and that this dinaturality is equivalent to naturality of the parametrized adjunction in p; then dualize.

items.name: triangle identities for a parametrized adjunction
items.statement_summary: Formulate the triangular (triangle) identities for an adjunction with a parameter.

items.name: dinaturality by separation of arguments
items.statement_summary: For S : (CxD)^op x C x D -> B and a family beta_{c,d} : S(c,d,c,d) -> b, show beta : S =.> b (dinatural to a constant b) is dinatural iff it is dinatural in c for each fixed d and dinatural in d for each fixed c; state the dual.

items.name: composition rule for more factors
items.statement_summary: Extend the composition rule of Proposition 1 (composite of two dinatural transformations along a middle variable) to S : C x C^op x C x C^op x C -> B, and to any odd number of factors C.

items.name: dinatural transformations need not compose
items.statement_summary: For S : C^op x C -> B and objects b, b', show that dinatural transformations b =.> S and S =.> b' do not in general have a well-defined composite b -> b'.

items.name: general composition of many-variable natural transformations
items.statement_summary: Extending Exercises 3 and 4, find a general rule for composing natural/dinatural transformations in many variables.

items.name: end of a functor
items.statement_summary: An end of S : C^op x C -> X is a universal wedge (dinatural transformation) <e, omega> from the constant e to S: omega : e =.> S such that every wedge beta : x =.> S factors uniquely as beta_a = omega_a . h through a unique h : x -> e. omega is the ending/universal wedge with components omega_c; the object e is written as the integral int_c S(c,c), the end of S.

items.name: set of natural transformations is an end of hom
items.statement_summary: For functors U, V : C -> X, hom_X(U-,V-) : C^op x C -> Set is a functor and a wedge from a set Y to it is exactly a Y-indexed natural family; hence the set of natural transformations equals the end Nat(U,V) = int_c hom_X(Uc,Vc) (eqn 2).

items.name: subdivision category C-section and functor S-section
items.statement_summary: The subdivision category of C: objects are symbols c-section (for objects c) and f-section (for arrows f), with, for each f : b -> c, two non-identity arrows b-section -> f-section <- c-section (only compositions with an identity factor exist). Each S : C^op x C -> X yields a functor S-section on this category with S-section(c-section)=S(c,c), S-section(f-section)=S(b,c), legs S(b,f) and S(f,c); cones over S-section correspond exactly to wedges over S.

items.name: end equals the limit of S-section (ends reduce to limits)
items.statement_summary: For S : C^op x C -> X with associated S-section on the subdivision category, there is an isomorphism int_c S(c,c) = Lim[S-section] (eqn 3): if either the end or the limit exists, so does the other, and the comparison arrow theta carrying the ending wedge to the limiting cone is an isomorphism.

items.name: existence of ends in a small-complete category
items.statement_summary: If X is small-complete and C is small, then every functor S : C^op x C -> X has an end in X.

items.name: every limit is an end
items.statement_summary: For T : C -> X let S = T . Q be the composite with Q : C^op x C -> C the second projection <c,c'> |-> c'. Then <e, tau : e =.> T> is a limit of T iff <e, tau : e =.> S> is an end of S; equivalently int_c Tc = Lim T (the end over a functor ignoring its first variable is the limit).

items.name: preservation and creation of an end by a functor
items.statement_summary: A functor H : X -> Y preserves the end of S : C^op x C -> X when omega : e =.> S being an end implies H.omega : He =.> HS is an end (H int_c S(c,c) = int_c HS(c,c)); H creates the end of S when every wedge v : y =.> HS lifts to a unique wedge omega : e =.> S with H.omega = v and that omega is an end of S.

items.name: hom-functors preserve and reverse ends
items.statement_summary: Hom-functors are continuous with respect to ends: for each object x, X(x, int_c S(c,c)) = int_c X(x, S(c,c)) (covariant hom preserves ends, eqn 4) and X(int^c S(c,c), x) = int_c X(S(c,c), x) (contravariant hom sends a coend to an end, eqn 5).

items.name: coend of a functor
items.statement_summary: A coend of S : C^op x C -> X is a universal wedge <d, zeta> from S to the constant d: zeta : S =.> d couniversal among dinatural transformations from S to constants. The object d (unique up to iso when it exists) is written with the integral int^c S(c,c) (bound variable as superscript). Dual to the end.

items.name: tensor product of modules is a coend
items.statement_summary: Viewing a ring R as a one-object Ab-category, a left R-module as an additive functor R -> Ab and a right R-module as an additive functor R^op -> Ab, the bifunctor A tensor B : R^op x R -> Ab has coend int^R A tensor B = A tensor_R B, the usual tensor product over R (M is the coend iff M is A tensor B modulo all ar tensor b - a tensor rb).

items.name: tensor product of functors (coend)
items.statement_summary: For a monoidal category (B, box) and functors T : P^op -> B and S : P -> B, their tensor product is defined as the coend T box_P S = int^P (Tp) box (Sp), an object of B (extending the module tensor product to any monoidal base).

items.name: geometric realization of a simplicial set is a coend
items.statement_summary: With Delta : SimplexCat -> Top realizing each ordinal n+1 as the n-dimensional affine simplex and a simplicial set S : SimplexCat^op -> Set, the assignment (n,m) |-> Sn . Delta m (copower) is a functor SimplexCat^op x SimplexCat -> Top whose coend int^n (Sn) . Delta n is the geometric realization of S (eqn 1).

items.name: set of wedges from a point is the end
items.statement_summary: For S : C^op x C -> Set, prove the set Wedge(*, S) of all wedges omega : * =.> S from the one-point set is an end of S, with ending wedge omega |-> omega_c(*) in S(c,c); compare with the explicit description of a limit in Set as a set of cones.

items.name: ends from products and equalizers
items.statement_summary: Show directly (without using limits) that a category X with all small products and all equalizers has all small ends (mirroring the products-plus-equalizers construction of limits).

items.name: twisted arrow category and reduction of ends to limits
items.statement_summary: Let the twisted arrow category of C have objects the arrows f : a -> b and morphisms <h,k> : f -> f' given by h : a' -> a (note the twist) and k : b -> b' with f' = k f h, and let K map it to C^op x C. For any S : C^op x C -> B, prove cones e -> SK correspond to wedges e =.> S, giving another proof of the reduction of ends to limits (Proposition 5.1).

items.name: free module as a coend
items.statement_summary: With Fin the skeletal category of finite nonempty ordinals and all functions, X^(-) : Fin^op -> Set (n |-> X^n) and R_1 : Fin -> R-Mod (n |-> R^n; a function f : n -> m sends basis vector a_j to a_{f(j)}, i.e. b_i = sum of a_j over the fiber f^{-1}(i)), show the free R-module on a set X is the coend int^n X^n . R_(n), recovering the description of elements as finite formal sums sum x_i a_i.

items.name: functor tensor product over a cocomplete category
items.statement_summary: If D is cocomplete, functors S : C^op -> Set and T : C -> D have a tensor product defined as the coend int^c (Sc) . (Tc) (copower); show it is a functor D^C x Set^{C^op} -> D.

items.name: end of a natural transformation (functoriality of ends)
items.statement_summary: Given gamma : S =.> S' between functors S, S' : C^op x C -> X both with ends <e,omega>, <e',omega'>, there is a unique arrow g = int_c gamma_{c,c} : e -> e' with omega'_c . g = gamma_{c,c} . omega_c for every c (eqn 1); moreover the composition rule int_c (gamma' . gamma)_{c,c} = (int_c gamma'_{c,c}) . (int_c gamma_{c,c}) holds, so taking ends is functorial.

items.name: Parameter Theorem for ends and limits
items.statement_summary: If T : P x C^op x C -> X is a functor such that T(p,-,-) has an end omega_p : int_c T(p,c,c) =.> T(p,-,-) for each object p in P (eqn 3), then there is a unique functor U : P -> X with object function Up = int_c T(p,c,c) such that each wedge component (omega_p)_c : Up -> T(p,c,c) is natural in p; written U = int_c T(-,c,c).

items.name: Parameter Theorem continued (parametrized end is an end in X^P)
items.statement_summary: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2, let T-section : C^op x C -> X^P be the transpose of T (T-section(f,f') = T(-,f,f')). Then the functor U = int_c T(-,c,c) is the end of T-section in the functor category X^P, with universal wedge omega-section whose components satisfy (omega-section_c)_p = (omega_p)_c for all p and c.

items.name: limit that is not a pointwise limit
items.statement_summary: (Dubuc.) Construct a functor category X^P and a functor T : C -> X^P having a limit that is not a pointwise limit (suggestion: take C = 2).

items.name: parameter theorem for coends
items.statement_summary: State and prove the parameter theorem for coends (dual of Theorems 2-3).

items.name: Lim is a functor
items.statement_summary: If X is small-complete and C is small, use Proposition 1 to prove that Lim : X^C -> X is a functor.

items.name: inclusion of discrete subcategory creates ends and coends
items.statement_summary: For any categories X and P, show the functor X^P -> X^{|P|} induced by including the discrete subcategory |P| creates ends and coends.

items.name: Fubini: double end equals iterated end
items.statement_summary: For S : P^op x P x C^op x C -> X such that the inner end int_c S(p,q,c,c) exists for all pairs <p,q> (a bifunctor P^op x P -> X), and S regarded as a bifunctor on (PxC), there is an isomorphism int_{<p,c>} S(p,p,c,c) = int_p int_c S(p,p,c,c): the double end exists iff the iterated end does, and the comparison theta is an isomorphism. Requires the inner end for all pairs <p,q>, not just p=q.

items.name: interchange of iterated ends (Fubini)
items.statement_summary: For S : P^op x P x C^op x C -> X such that the ends int_c S(p,q,c,c) and int_p S(p,p,b,c) exist for all p,q,b,c, the two iterated ends are isomorphic: int_p int_c S(p,p,c,c) = int_c int_p S(p,p,c,c); one exists iff the other does and theta is the unique comparison isomorphism.

items.name: interchange of iterated limits and colimits
items.statement_summary: Specializing the Fubini corollary to a functor F : P x C -> X with P, C small and X complete gives the interchange of iterated limits Lim_p Lim_c F(p,c) = Lim_{<p,c>} F(p,c) = Lim_c Lim_p F(p,c), with the dual formula for colimits.
